text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: inferpool-us-east-1-a high node churn (NotReady) + serving-runtime OOMs. Pagerduty: P2 - automated escalations sent.

sara_oncall: seeing a NotReady spike in us-east-1-a, ~6 nodes flipped within last 3m. routing shows increased 5xxs for /v1/generate.

kai_infra: checking kubelet logs now, getting repeated `kubelet: Heartbeat missed` and `kubelet: container runtime stopped` around the same timestamps.

miguel_sre: on the serving side we're also seeing CUDA driver reset on two GPU nodes, and a couple pods crashed with OOMKilled in the last minute. stacktraces point to kv-cache growth on long-context requests.

jules_prod: customers: a couple of high-traffic tenants reported elevated latency and some 429s; SLO alert on p95 tokens/latency tripped. Estimated impact: ~4% of total requests, concentrated in us-east-1-a.

sara_oncall: quick mitigation plan: cordon the flaky nodes, drain what we can, and steer traffic to inferpool-us-east-1-b/c. also reduce model batch_size or fallback to smaller variant for the rest of the pool.

kai_infra: agree. I'll cordon nodes n-23, n-24, n-27 that show repeated kubelet restarts. running:
```bash
kubectl cordon node-n-23
kubectl drain node-n-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

miguel_sre: while you drain, I'll push a temporary route override to reduce per-request batch to 1 for suspect model routes (model: redwood-7b/v1) to lower memory pressure. patching routing config in console now.

ops_bot: Route update pushed: `route:infer-7b` -> batch_size=1 (canary: 10% -> 100% once validated).

alex_support: notified the two impacted customers via status page (US-EAST degraded), added note: engineering investigating.

sara_oncall: Kai, any sign this is driver-level (NVIDIA) vs something in kubelet?

kai_infra: logs show both `nvidia-mig: failed to initialize` followed by `kernel: nvidia: XXX reset` and kubelet reaped containers. I'm leaning driver instability triggered by high GPU memory churn.

miguel_sre: also saw a KV cache pinning bug yesterday that could make long sequences allocate more GPU memory. Rolling the lower batch_size should reduce chance of OOMs. I'll open a hotfix PR to cap kv-cache at runtime.

sara_oncall: good. For immediate traffic: jules, can you shift traffic for customer-facing routes to dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-us-east-1) and enable graceful fallback to quantized model variant?

jules_prod: doing now. Patching routing policy: prefer dedicated pool, fallback to model-quant-7b if request exceeds 2s latency.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3248. Severity: P2. Slack thread auto-attached.

kai_infra: drain in progress, two pods evicted, one pod failed to terminate due to crashloop - collecting pod logs:
```text
container runtime out of memory: killed process 1 (server) signal 9
CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
```
Saving logs to s3://redwood-ops/logs/6491204820/node-n-24.log

miguel_sre: after lowering batch_size, we're seeing reduced OOMs in logs and latency for the fallback routes is stable. canary traffic at 10% looks good for 2 minutes.

sara_oncall: good. keep drains going, don't reboot nodes yet. If driver resets persist after drain, we'll escalate to kernel/driver upgrade window.

alex_support: updated status page: "Partial degradation in US-EAST (mitigations in flight)." Added note that some requests may see retries or fallback to lower-throughput models.

jules_prod: traffic now at 80% moved to dedicated pool, 20% to fallback quantized variant. visible p95 latency back to normal for affected customers.

ops_bot: Autoscaler: no extra nodes launched because cluster has reached soft quota in that AZ. Requesting manual quota bump or steer traffic.

sara_oncall: don't increase cluster size for now. prefer cross-AZ steer. Kai, open support ticket with cloud provider if driver resets continue after drains.

kai_infra: on it.Filed ticket CNTRL-44212 with cloud provider, attaching kernel and dmesg logs.

miguel_sre: action items for post-incident: 1) hotfix to cap kv-cache memory, 2) add kubelet readiness threshold bump to avoid tight notready oscillation alerts, 3) review driver update plan for nodes that showed resets. I'll own the kv-cache PR.

sara_oncall: handoff in 30m to night oncall @mila_oncall. I'll write a short runbook of what we did and what to watch. Please keep console routing locked until we confirm stable for 1h.

alex_support: customers notified on status page and via 1:1 for the two tenants. will keep updates until cleared.

incident-bot: Pager cleared: automated paging ended, incident remains open for investigation.

sara_oncall: summary: kubelet heartbeat hiccup caused node flaps in us-east-1-a which coincided with CUDA driver resets and serving runtime OOMs on a subset of GPU pods. Mitigations: cordon/drain flaky nodes, steer traffic to dedicated pools + fallback quantized models, lower batch_size patch pushed. Impact: ~4% requests affected, two tenants had transient 429s - no data loss observed. Next: kv-cache cap hotfix + driver postmortem.

jules_prod: I'll prep postmortem template and add timeline. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

mila_oncall: (acknowledged) I'll pick this up for follow-up, please DM if anything regresses.
